newsitem.title: CHINA: CHINA PREPARING UNIFIED LAW ON ASSETS APPRAISAL.
newsitem.headline: CHINA PREPARING UNIFIED LAW ON ASSETS APPRAISAL.

text.p: China is preparing a unified law on asset appraisal that could help to boost capital movement by guarding against asset erosion, an official of the National Administration of State Property said on Monday.

Legislation was needed to strengthen the supervision of asset appraisals and to allow enterprises to make fuller legitimate use of their assets, said Li Chunman of the administration's department of policy and regulation.

Officials were preparing the law, which would replace a slew of disparate rules and regulations covering the appraisal of assets held by both state and non-state enterprises, Li told Reuters at a seminar organised by the property administration.
It was unclear when the law would be approved or go into force, he said.

Chinese officials have long expressed grave concern that huge amounts of state property are being siphoned into private hands as reforms transform ownership patterns in the once uniformly state-owned economy.
Changes of asset ownership were necessary, but it was vital to ensure that state property was properly valued to guard against its loss, Li said.
"Movement and erosion are two different things," he said. "Capital can only be effective and grow if it is allowed to move -- but movement creates the high possibility of losses," he said.
